subject: Preemption window proposal & soft-reserve offer — Vertex Labs launch
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@vertexlabs.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@vertexlabs.ai
Date: 2028-06-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity outlook & potential preemption risk for Vertex Labs

Hi Rishi,

Quick note as we head toward our public beta next month — our traffic profile has a lot of burstiness: daily spikes during business hours and a few larger waves around product announcements. Your team quoted a dedicated sizing recommendation (120 GPUs peak, 60 steady), but procurement flagged the language around potential preemption during fleet congestion.

Two asks: 1) can you confirm whether our launch windows would be at risk of preemption, and 2) if so, what mitigations you can offer (reserved windows, burst credits, or an SLA carve-out)? We’re finalizing the launch ops runbook and need clarity for the infra appendix.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Engineering, Vertex Labs
Alicia.Gomez@vertexlabs.ai

---
Attachment: traffic_profile_q2.csv (attachment stub)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@vertexlabs.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity outlook & potential preemption risk for Vertex Labs

Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads-up and for the traffic CSV. Short answer: with current commitments on our fleet we do anticipate preemption risk during high-congestion windows unless we apply one of the mitigations below. Summary of options we can implement quickly: 

- Soft reservation (recommended): carve a rolling soft-reserve of 48-64 GPUs for Vertex during defined launch windows (you pick 4-hour blocks). Preemption inside the block is deprioritized; in extreme overload we may still move to preempt but with 30-minute advance notice and migration guidance.
- Burst credits: keep your committed 60 GPUs steady and provide a pool of 60 burst-GPU credits usable at 2x throughput, consumed first before preemption. Credits are billable at a premium rate but guarantee capacity without changing baseline commit.
- SLA amendment / paid carve-out: a contractual dedicated tranche (min 96 GPUs guaranteed) with higher monthly commit and explicit non-preemption SLA. This avoids preemption but requires procurement sign-off and billing adjustments.

I’ve attached a short preemption_plan_v1.pdf that lays out tradeoffs, implementation steps, and expected cost delta for each approach. Practically, the fastest path for a launch in 4–6 weeks is the soft reservation + burst credits combo.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute slot later today to pick windows and hammer out the numbers; otherwise I can circulate a proposed windows matrix for your ops team to confirm.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Director, Dedicated Capacity — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Preemption window proposal & soft-reserve offer — Vertex Labs

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick triage and the options. A couple of leadership notes before we finalize a customer-facing proposal: 

1) Avoid promising anything that materially changes our enterprise SLA without commercial sign-off. If we move to a non-preemptible carve-out at reduced price, that’s a concession we must track to renewal economics.
2) Prefer the soft-reservation + burst credit approach for a beta customer — it balances risk and preserves operational flexibility. However, we should quantify: expected impact to other customers (headroom burn), fallback behaviors, and a clear rollback plan.
3) Engage legal/sales-ops for an amendment template if Vertex wants the SLA carve-out. Ben, please prepare a redline-ready amendment with a term sheet showing cost delta for: 48 GPU soft-reserve, 96 GPU guaranteed tranche, and 120 GPU guaranteed tranche.

I’m copying Vivek to flag potential deal-class escalation — if Vertex pushes for a guaranteed tranche at the same price as commit, escalate to me and we’ll take to CRO.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product & GTM Operations — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Date: 2028-06-02T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preemption window proposal & soft-reserve offer — Vertex Labs

Hi Alicia — following internal alignment, here’s a concrete proposal your team can review today: 

Proposal (fast path, launch-safe):
- Baseline commit: 60 GPUs steady (as previously quoted).
- Soft-reserve: schedule two daily launch windows (Monday–Friday) of 4 hours each where we hold 48 GPUs as soft-reserve for Vertex. We will not preempt those GPUs during the window except for catastrophic events; if preemption becomes necessary, we will provide 30-minute notice and target non-disruptive KV-migration.
- Burst credits: a pool of 48 GPU-hours per day that can be consumed in bursts at a 2x throughput factor. Credits are billed at a 1.5x premium over base per-GPU hour. Unused credits roll over weekly for the first three weeks post-launch.

Operational notes: we’ll instrument per-route tracing for your job patterns, enable prefix KV caching on the critical traffic paths, and provide a daily headroom report for the first 30 days. Implementation timeline: we can enable the soft-reserve + burst credits in 72 hours once we have the signed amendment.

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm the two daily 4-hour windows (local times) or give an alternate matrix.
2) Confirm acceptance of the temporary credit billing profile.
3) Sign the attached amendment (amendment_vertexlabs_v1.pdf) or indicate requested redlines; I’ve included a DocuSign link in related links for faster turn.

If you’d prefer a guaranteed (non-preemptible) tranche, we can price that separately — Ben, Vivek, and I will follow up with a term sheet as Laura requested.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you launch-ready.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Director, Dedicated Capacity — Redwood Inference
